Chapter 1: How Local SEO Works for Home Service Businesses

Local SEO is the practice of optimizing your online presence to attract more business from relevant local searches. For home service businesses, it means showing up when a homeowner types "emergency plumber near me" or "HVAC repair Dallas" into Google.

Here's the thing: local SEO for contractors works differently than local SEO for retail stores. Understanding these differences is the foundation everything else builds on.

The Local Pack vs. Organic Results

When someone searches for a home service, Google displays results in three distinct zones:

Result Type Position Click-Through Rate Best For
Local Pack (Map Pack) Top of page, below ads 42% of all local clicks Immediate service needs
Organic results Below the map 33% of clicks Research-phase searches
Paid ads (LSA/PPC) Very top 25% of clicks Emergency/high-intent queries

The Local Pack is a map with three business listings. It appears in 93% of local service searches, according to BrightLocal's 2025 research. For contractors, this is where the money is. A homeowner with a burst pipe does not scroll past the map to read blog posts. They click the first plumber they see.

The organic results below the map matter too, especially for higher-consideration services like roofing or solar installation. But the Local Pack captures the majority of emergency and same-day service calls.

Service-Area Business vs. Brick-and-Mortar

This distinction changes everything about your strategy.

Factor Brick-and-Mortar (Retail, Restaurant) Service-Area Business (Contractor, HVAC, Plumbing)
Primary ranking factor Proximity to searcher Prominence and relevance
Address display Public, visible on map Hidden, service areas defined by city/ZIP
Google Maps pin Visible location No pin; service area polygon
Review importance Important Critical — weighted more heavily in algorithm
Content focus Location, amenities, hours Service areas, proof of work, expertise
Customer journey Visit store, browse, buy Call, schedule, service at home
Conversion event Foot traffic, in-store purchase Phone call, form fill, booking

Brick-and-mortar businesses win when they are physically close to the searcher. A pizza shop three blocks away outranks a better pizza shop ten miles away. For contractors, proximity still matters, but it is not the deciding factor. Google knows a plumber can drive 20 miles. What matters more is whether Google trusts that plumber to do good work.

That trust comes from three pillars: relevance (does your profile match the search?), prominence (are you well-known and well-reviewed online?), and proximity (are you reasonably close to the searcher?). For service-area businesses, prominence and relevance carry far more weight than they do for storefronts.

How Homeowners Search for Contractors

Understanding the search patterns of your customers lets you optimize for the exact moments they need you.

Emergency searches (highest intent, highest conversion):
- "emergency plumber near me"
- "24 hour HVAC repair [city]"
- "water damage restoration open now"

These searches happen on mobile, often at night or on weekends. 76% of local searches result in a phone call within 24 hours, and 28% result in a purchase within that same window, according to Google. For emergency services, the conversion rate can exceed 15%.

Planned service searches (medium intent, research phase):
- "roof replacement cost [city]"
- "best solar company in [city]"
- "HVAC installation near me"

These searches happen during business hours, often on desktop. The homeowner is comparing options, reading reviews, and getting multiple quotes. They may visit your website, read your blog, and check your portfolio before calling.

Maintenance and seasonal searches (lower intent, relationship building):
- "AC tune up [city]"
- "gutter cleaning near me"
- "annual furnace maintenance"

These searches build long-term customer relationships. The homeowner who books an annual maintenance plan today calls you first when their system fails next summer.

The Local Search Algorithm Explained Simply

Google's local algorithm evaluates hundreds of signals, but they cluster into seven categories. Here is how the weight breaks down for service-area businesses in 2026, based on the latest Whitespark Local Search Ranking Factors survey:

Ranking Factor Category Weight What It Means for Contractors
Google Business Profile signals 32% Category choice, business description, photos, posts, Q&A, services
Review signals 20% Quantity, recency, rating, text content, owner responses
On-page signals 15% Location pages, service pages, NAP consistency, schema markup
Behavioral signals 9% Click-through rate, calls, direction requests, profile engagement
Link signals 8% Quality and relevance of inbound links
Citation signals 6% NAP consistency across directories
Personalization 6% Searcher's location, search history, device
Social signals 4% Social media mentions and engagement

Key insight: GBP optimization and reviews alone account for 52% of your ranking potential. If you do nothing else, nail these two categories and you will outperform most of your competitors. 56% of Google Business Profiles are not fully optimized, according to Visionary Marketing. Simply completing every field puts you ahead of half the market.

Key Ranking Factors Overview

Before we dive into tactics, here are the specific signals that matter most for contractors:

  1. Primary business category — The #1 most important factor. Choosing "HVAC contractor" instead of "contractor" can be the difference between page one and page three.
  2. Keywords in business title — Businesses with service keywords in their name (e.g., "Johnson Plumbing") rank significantly higher. Do not stuff keywords, but if your legal name includes your trade, use it.
  3. Review quantity with text — 200+ reviews is the milestone for consistent top-3 Local Pack placement. Aim for 10+ new reviews per month.
  4. Review recency — The most recent review on your profile should be no older than two weeks. Fresh reviews signal an active, trusted business.
  5. Dedicated service pages on your website — A page for each service you offer, optimized for "[service] + [city]," is the #1 organic local ranking factor.
  6. NAP consistency — Your name, address, and phone number must match character-for-character across your website, GBP, and every directory.
  7. LocalBusiness schema markup — Structured data helps Google understand your business type, service area, hours, and services.

Chapter 2: Google Business Profile Optimization

Your Google Business Profile (GBP) is the single most important asset in your local SEO strategy. It is not a directory listing. It is your digital storefront, your 24/7 salesperson, and your primary lead generator. A complete GBP gets 7 times more clicks than an incomplete one, according to Google.

This chapter covers every element of GBP optimization specifically for service-area businesses. Follow it step by step, and you will have a profile that outranks 90% of your competitors.

Setting Up GBP for Service-Area Businesses

The setup process for contractors differs from brick-and-mortar businesses in one critical way: you must hide your address.

Step 1: Choose the correct business type
When creating your profile, select "Service-area business" instead of "Storefront." This tells Google you visit customers at their locations rather than receiving walk-in traffic.

Step 2: Hide your address
After verification, go to your profile settings and check the box that says "Hide my address (it's not a store)." Your address will still be visible to Google for verification purposes, but customers will not see it on your profile or map listing.

Step 3: Define your service areas
Google allows you to define up to 20 service areas by city, ZIP code, or region. Do not use a radius. Specific cities and ZIP codes give Google clearer signals about where you work.

Best practice: List your primary city first, followed by the next 10-15 cities and ZIP codes you actively serve. Do not claim an entire state from a single location. Keep your service areas within approximately a two-hour driving radius. Unrealistic service areas trigger Google's spam filters.

Step 4: Verify your profile
Google will send a postcard to your business address with a verification code. This typically takes 5-14 business days. Some businesses qualify for phone or email verification. Until verified, your profile will not appear in search results.

[VISUAL: Google Business Profile setup checklist infographic showing each step with checkboxes]

Category Selection by Trade

Your primary business category is the #1 ranking factor for local search. Choose wrong, and you are invisible. Choose right, and you unlock targeted traffic.

Google offers hundreds of categories, but only one primary category per profile. You can add up to nine secondary categories.

Primary category recommendations by trade:

Trade Recommended Primary Category Secondary Categories to Add
Plumbing Plumber Drain cleaning service, Water damage restoration service, Emergency plumbing service
HVAC HVAC contractor Air conditioning contractor, Heating contractor, Air conditioning repair service
Roofing Roofing contractor Roof repair service, Gutter cleaning service, Siding contractor
Electrical Electrician Electrical installation service, Emergency electrician, Lighting contractor
Solar Solar energy company Solar panel installer, Energy consultant, Roofing contractor
Restoration Water damage restoration service Mold remediation service, Fire damage restoration service, Construction company
Landscaping Landscaper Lawn care service, Tree service, Irrigation system contractor
Pest Control Pest control service Termite control service, Exterminator, Animal control service
Painting Painting House painter, Commercial painter, Drywall contractor
Flooring Flooring contractor Carpet installer, Tile contractor, Hardwood floor contractor

Critical rule: Your primary category must match the service you want to rank for most. If you are a plumber who also does HVAC, choose "Plumber" as your primary if plumbing generates 70% of your revenue. You can create a separate GBP for your HV

AC division if both are substantial.

Pro tip: Search your primary keyword in Google and look at what categories the top three Local Pack results use. Google the category name plus your city to see who ranks. This competitive intelligence tells you exactly what Google expects.

Service Area Configuration

Service areas tell Google where you are willing to travel. They also tell homeowners whether you serve their neighborhood.

How to configure service areas:

  1. Start with your home base city — This is where you have the strongest proximity signal.
  2. Add adjacent cities — List cities in order of importance to your business.
  3. Include ZIP codes for precision — For large metro areas, ZIP codes give Google more granular data than city names alone.
  4. Update seasonally — If you expand into a new market or stop serving a distant area, update your service areas immediately.

Common mistake: Listing 20 random cities across a 200-mile radius. Google sees this as spam. Be realistic about where you actually send technicians.

Business Description Optimization

Your GBP business description has a 750-character limit. Every character should work.

Formula for a high-converting description:

[Business name] is a [trade] serving [primary city] and [surrounding areas]. 
We specialize in [top 2-3 services] with [key differentiator: 24/7 availability, 
20+ years experience, licensed and insured, etc.]. [Social proof: 500+ 5-star reviews, 
BBB A+ rated]. Call [phone number] for [primary CTA: free estimate, emergency service, etc.].

Example for a plumber:

"ClearFlow Plumbing is a licensed plumber serving Dallas, Plano, Richardson, and Frisco. We specialize in emergency plumbing repair, drain cleaning, and water heater installation with 24/7 availability and same-day service. With over 500 five-star Google reviews and a BBB A+ rating, we are the trusted choice for homeowners across North Texas. Call (214) 555-0199 for a free estimate."

What to include:
- Your primary service keyword naturally
- Your primary city and 2-3 surrounding cities
- Your top services
- A credibility signal (reviews, years in business, licensing)
- A phone number (clickable on mobile)
- A clear call to action

What to avoid:
- Keyword stuffing
- All caps
- Promotional language ("best," "cheapest")
- URLs (they are not clickable in the description)
- Special characters or emojis

Photo Strategy for Contractors

Photos are not optional. Businesses with photos on their GBP receive 42% more requests for driving directions and 35% more website clicks than businesses without photos, according to Google.

The contractor photo checklist:

Photo Type Quantity Purpose
Logo 1 Brand recognition
Team/owner photo 2-3 Trust and personality
Service vehicle 2-3 Professionalism and branding
Before/after project photos 10-20+ Proof of work quality
Team at work 5-10 Shows real people doing real work
Office/shop 2-3 Legitimacy (even if SAB)
Equipment/tools 3-5 Expertise and capability
Happy customers 5-10 Social proof (with permission)

Photo optimization tips:
- Geo-tag your photos before uploading. Use tools like GeoImgr or the Exif data editor on your phone. Photos with GPS coordinates embedded signal local relevance to Google.
- Use descriptive filenames. Rename photos before upload: dallas-kitchen-remodel-before.jpg instead of IMG_2345.jpg.
- Upload 5-10 new photos per month. Fresh photos signal an active business.
- Add captions. When uploading through the GBP dashboard, add brief captions describing the project and location.
- Include video. Short 30-second project walkthroughs perform exceptionally well.

Post Strategy

Google Posts are free mini-ads that appear on your GBP. They expire after seven days, which means you should post weekly to maintain visibility.

Post types that work for contractors:

  1. What's New — Share a recent project completion with before/after photos.
  2. Offers — Promote seasonal discounts ("$50 off AC tune-ups this month").
  3. Events — Announce free homeowner workshops or community events.
  4. Products — Highlight specific services with pricing.

Post formula:
- Headline: 4-5 words with a benefit ("New Roof Installation in Frisco")
- Body: 1-2 sentences describing the project or offer
- Call to action button: "Call now," "Book online," or "Learn more"
- Photo: High-quality image related to the post

Posting schedule: One post per week minimum. The businesses that post weekly see 70% more engagement than those that post monthly or less, according to Google.

Q&A Optimization

The Q&A section on your GBP is one of the most underutilized ranking factors. It is also a prime opportunity to place location and service keywords naturally.

How to optimize Q&A:

  1. Seed the first 10 questions yourself. Log out of your Google account (or use a different Google account) and ask common questions. Then answer them from your business account.
  2. Include keywords in questions and answers. For example:
  3. Q: "Do you offer emergency plumbing service in Plano?"
  4. A: "Yes, we provide 24/7 emergency plumbing repair throughout Plano, Frisco, and McKinney. Our technicians typically arrive within 60 minutes. Call (214) 555-0199 anytime."
  5. Monitor and answer new questions within 24 hours. Google sends notifications when someone asks a question on your profile.
  6. Upvote your own seeded questions. Questions with more upvotes appear first.

10 seeded questions every contractor should add:

  1. Do you offer [primary service] in [city]? — Include your top city.
  2. What areas do you serve? — List all service areas.
  3. Are you licensed and insured? — State your credentials.
  4. Do you offer free estimates? — Clarify your pricing approach.
  5. What are your business hours? — Include emergency availability.
  6. How quickly can you respond to emergencies? — Set expectations.
  7. Do you warranty your work? — Mention warranty terms.
  8. What payment methods do you accept? — Remove friction.
  9. Can I see examples of your past work? — Link to your portfolio.
  10. How do I schedule service? — Make it easy to book.

Product/Service Listings

Google now allows you to list specific services with descriptions and pricing directly on your GBP. This is especially powerful for contractors because it matches your profile to specific service searches.

How to add services:

  1. Go to your GBP dashboard.
  2. Click "Services" in the left menu.
  3. Add each service you offer with a description of 300-1,000 characters.
  4. Include pricing if possible (even a range like "$150-$300").

Service description formula:

[Service name] in [primary city] and surrounding areas. Our [trade] technicians 
are licensed, insured, and experienced in [specific details]. We offer 
[benefit: same-day service, 24/7 availability, free estimates]. 
Call [phone] to schedule.

Example:

"Emergency Drain Cleaning in Dallas and surrounding areas. Our licensed plumbers use professional-grade equipment to clear clogged drains, sewer lines, and grease traps. We offer same-day service and 24/7 emergency response. Call (214) 555-0199 to schedule."

Add 10-20 services covering every offering you have. The more services you list, the more search queries your profile can match.

Chapter 3: Review Generation and Management

Reviews are the second-most important ranking factor for local SEO, accounting for approximately 20% of your Local Pack ranking weight. But reviews are more than a ranking signal. They are social proof that converts searchers into callers.

87% of consumers read online reviews before choosing a local business, and 88% trust reviews as much as personal recommendations, according to BrightLocal's 2026 Local Consumer Review Survey. For contractors, reviews are often the deciding factor between you and the competitor ranked one spot below you.

Why Reviews Matter for Contractors

The impact of reviews on your business goes far beyond rankings. Here is what the data shows:

Review Factor Impact
Consumers who read reviews before hiring 87-88%
Consumers who trust reviews like personal recommendations 88%
Consumers who won't consider businesses below 4.0 stars 57%
Revenue increase per 0.1 star improvement Up to 25%
Businesses with 50+ reviews more likely in Local Pack 266% more likely
Review "sweet spot" for consumer trust 4.2-4.5 stars
Consumers who read business responses to reviews 97%

The contractor-specific review advantage: Home service businesses consistently earn the highest average ratings on Google compared to other industries. HVAC companies average 4.55 stars, plumbers average 4.52 stars, and electricians average 4.50 stars, according to ReplyOnTheFly's 2026 industry benchmarks. Homeowners appreciate contractors who show up on time, solve their problem, and leave their home clean. The bar for a five-star review in home services is surprisingly achievable.

Review Generation Scripts

The #1 reason contractors do not have enough reviews is simple: they do not ask. Most satisfied customers will leave a review if you make it easy. Here are the exact scripts that work.

Script 1: In-person ask (most effective)

"[Customer name], I'm so glad we could get your [problem] fixed today. If you have 30 seconds, would you mind leaving us a quick review on Google? It really helps other homeowners in [city] find us. I can send you a link by text right now."

Script 2: Text message follow-up (sent 2-4 hours after job completion)

"Hi [Name], this is [Your name] from [Business]. Thanks again for choosing us for your [service] today. If you were happy with our work, would you mind leaving a quick Google review? It takes 30 seconds and helps us a ton. [short link]"

Script 3: Email follow-up (sent 24 hours after service)

Subject: How did we do with your [service]?

Hi [Name],

I hope your [service] is working perfectly. We enjoyed working with you in [neighborhood].

If you have a moment, would you leave us a review on Google? Your feedback helps other homeowners in [city] make confident decisions.

[Review link button]

Thank you,
[Your name]
[Business name]

Script 4: Invoice/receipt insert

"We hope you were 100% satisfied with your service today. If so, we'd be grateful for a quick Google review. Scan the QR code or visit [link]. Thank you for supporting local business!"

Script 5: Post-service card (left on counter or mailed)

"Your opinion matters! Help other [city] homeowners find trusted [trade] services. Leave your review at [link] or scan the QR code. As a thank you, enjoy 10% off your next service."

Timing and Automation

Timing is everything in review generation. Ask too early, and the customer has not experienced the full result. Ask too late, and they have forgotten about you.

Optimal timing by service type:

Service Type Best Time to Ask Why
Emergency repair 2-4 hours after completion Emotion is high; relief creates positive association
Scheduled maintenance Immediately after service Customer is present and satisfied
Large project (roofing, remodel) 1-3 days after completion Customer has seen the finished result
Recurring service After 3rd visit Relationship is established; customer is loyal

Automation tools for review generation:

Tool Best For Price Range
BirdEye Enterprise multi-location $300+/month
Podium Mid-size with SMS focus $200-400/month
Grade.us Simple review funnel $100-200/month
LocalVox Small business budget $50-100/month
Manual system Single-location startups Free (Google review link + spreadsheet)

The free manual system:
1. Create a Google review link from your GBP dashboard.
2. Shorten it with a branded short URL (bit.ly/yourbusiness-review).
3. Add the link to your email signature.
4. Text it to customers 2-4 hours after service.
5. Track requests and responses in a simple spreadsheet.

Responding to Negative Reviews

Every contractor gets a negative review eventually. How you respond matters more than the review itself. 97% of consumers read business responses to reviews, and a professional response to a negative review can actually increase trust.

The negative review response formula:

1. Acknowledge and apologize (even if you disagree)
2. Explain briefly without being defensive
3. Take the conversation offline
4. Offer to make it right

Example response:

"[Customer name], we're truly sorry your experience did not meet the standard we hold ourselves to. We take your feedback seriously and have already discussed this with our team. Please call our office at [phone] and ask for [manager name] so we can make this right. We value your business and hope to earn back your trust."

Rules for negative review responses:
- Respond within 24-48 hours.
- Never argue or blame the customer publicly.
- Never mention specifics that violate privacy (prices, contract details).
- Keep it brief — 3-4 sentences maximum.
- Use the customer's name to show you read their review.

Review Platform Strategy

Google reviews are the most important, but a diverse review profile builds trust and protects against platform-specific issues.

Platform priority for contractors:

Platform Priority Why
Google #1 — Essential Directly impacts Local Pack rankings; 73% of all reviews
Yelp #2 — Important High domain authority; consumers trust Yelp for service businesses
BBB #3 — Valuable Trust signal for older demographics; helps with licensing
Facebook #4 — Supplemental Social proof for Facebook users; easy to request
Industry-specific #5 — Niche Angi, Thumbtack, Houzz — trade-specific credibility

Focus 80% of your effort on Google reviews. The other platforms matter, but Google reviews directly move your Local Pack ranking. Once you have 50+ Google reviews, diversify to Yelp and BBB.

Review Velocity and Consistency

Google rewards businesses that earn reviews consistently over time, not in sporadic bursts.

Review velocity benchmarks:

Business Stage Target Reviews Per Month Target Total Reviews
New business (0-6 months) 5-10 30-60
Growing business (6-18 months) 10-15 100-200
Established business (18+ months) 10-20 200+
Market leader 15-25 500+

The "review burst" problem: If you go six months with no reviews and then get 20 in one week, Google may flag this as suspicious. A steady stream of

2-3 reviews per week looks natural and builds sustained ranking improvement.

Pro tip: Encourage customers to mention specific details in their reviews — the neighborhood, the type of service, the technician's name. Reviews that say "Mike fixed our AC in Plano same day" carry more local SEO weight than "Great service, highly recommend."

Chapter 4: On-Page Local SEO

Your website is the foundation that supports everything else. A perfectly optimized Google Business Profile sends traffic to a weak website, and that traffic bounces. A strong website reinforces your GBP signals and captures organic traffic the Local Pack misses.

This chapter covers the on-page elements that matter most for service-area businesses.

Location Page Architecture

Location pages are dedicated pages on your website targeting "[service] + [city]" searches. They are the #1 organic local ranking factor and one of the highest-ROI content investments you can make.

The location page formula:

URL: /locations/[city-name]/
H1: [Primary Service] in [City], [State]
Word count: 800-1,500 words

Required elements for every location page:

Element Purpose
Unique H1 "Plumbing Services in Dallas, TX" — not "Dallas Plumbing"
Intro paragraph 100-150 words about serving this specific city
Service list Link to each service you offer in this city
Local proof Projects completed, neighborhoods served, local landmarks
Customer testimonial Review from a customer in this city
Embedded map Google Map showing your service area
NAP block Name, address, phone — matching GBP exactly
Local schema LocalBusiness + Service markup
CTA Click-to-call phone number, booking form

The thin content trap: Simply swapping city names on a template page triggers Google's duplicate content penalty. Each location page must have genuinely unique content. Here is how to make them unique:

  • Mention specific neighborhoods you serve within that city.
  • Reference local landmarks or events ("We have been serving the Oak Lawn neighborhood near Turtle Creek for 15 years").
  • Include a unique customer story or testimonial from that city.
  • Describe city-specific challenges ("Dallas homes built before 1980 often have galvanized steel pipes that corrode").
  • Show photos from actual projects in that city.

Service area page strategy: If you serve 15 cities, create location pages for your top 5-7 cities. For smaller surrounding towns, create service area pages that group 2-3 nearby communities together.

Service Page Local Optimization

Every service you offer needs its own dedicated page. A single "Services" page with a bulleted list is not enough.

Service page structure:

URL: /services/[service-name]/
H1: [Service Name] in [Primary City] | [Business Name]
Word count: 1,000-2,000 words

Service page sections:

  1. What this service is — Direct answer for voice search and AI Overviews.
  2. Who needs it — Qualify the reader and build relevance.
  3. Your process — Step-by-step breakdown of how you deliver the service.
  4. Why choose you — Differentiators, credentials, guarantees.
  5. Pricing information — Even a range builds trust and captures price-comparison searches.
  6. FAQs — 5-10 common questions with concise answers.
  7. Related services — Internal links to complementary services.
  8. CTA — Phone number, form, or booking button.

Local optimization for service pages:
- Include your primary city naturally 3-5 times in the content.
- Mention 2-3 surrounding cities in the "Areas We Serve" section.
- Add a "Recent [Service] Projects in [City]" section with photos.
- Include LocalBusiness schema with service area markup.

NAP Consistency

NAP stands for Name, Address, Phone number. Consistency across every online mention of your business is critical for local SEO.

The NAP consistency rule: Your business name, address, and phone number must match character-for-character across your website, Google Business Profile, and every directory listing.

Common NAP inconsistencies that destroy rankings:

Inconsistent Element Example Problem Correct Approach
Business name "Johnson Plumbing" vs. "Johnson Plumbing LLC" vs. "Johnson Plumbing Inc." Pick one legal name and use it everywhere
Street address "123 Main St" vs. "123 Main Street" vs. "123 N Main St" Choose one format and stick to it
Suite/unit "Suite 100" vs. "Ste 100" vs. "#100" Standardize abbreviations
Phone number "(214) 555-0199" vs. "214-555-0199" vs. "214.555.0199" Use parentheses and dashes consistently
Website URL "https://" vs. "http://" vs. trailing slash variations Choose one and redirect all others

Create a "Single Source of Truth" document:

Business Name: [Exact legal name]
Address Line 1: [Exact street address]
Address Line 2: [Suite/unit if applicable]
City: [City name]
State: [Two-letter abbreviation]
ZIP: [Full ZIP code]
Phone: [(XXX) XXX-XXXX]
Website: [Exact URL]

Copy and paste from this document every time you create a new listing. Never retype your NAP from memory.

Schema Markup for Local Businesses

Schema markup is structured data code that helps search engines understand your business information. For local SEO, it is essential.

The three schema types every contractor needs:

1. LocalBusiness schema (homepage and location pages):

{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Plumber",
  "@id": "https://yoursite.com/#business",
  "name": "ClearFlow Plumbing",
  "url": "https://yoursite.com",
  "telephone": "+1-214-555-0199",
  "image": "https://yoursite.com/logo.png",
  "priceRange": "$$",
  "address": {
    "@type": "PostalAddress",
    "streetAddress": "123 Main St",
    "addressLocality": "Dallas",
    "addressRegion": "TX",
    "postalCode": "75201",
    "addressCountry": "US"
  },
  "geo": {
    "@type": "GeoCoordinates",
    "latitude": 32.77900,
    "longitude": -96.80000
  },
  "areaServed": ["Dallas", "Plano", "Richardson", "Frisco"],
  "openingHours": ["Mo-Fr 08:00-18:00", "Sa 09:00-13:00"],
  "sameAs": [
    "https://maps.google.com/?cid=1234567890",
    "https://www.facebook.com/clearflowplumbing"
  ]
}

2. Service schema (service pages):

{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Service",
  "name": "Emergency Drain Cleaning",
  "provider": {
    "@type": "Plumber",
    "name": "ClearFlow Plumbing"
  },
  "areaServed": {
    "@type": "City",
    "name": "Dallas"
  },
  "description": "24/7 emergency drain cleaning services in Dallas and surrounding areas."
}

3. FAQ schema (service pages and FAQ pages):

{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [{
    "@type": "Question",
    "name": "Do you offer emergency plumbing in Dallas?",
    "acceptedAnswer": {
      "@type": "Answer",
      "text": "Yes, ClearFlow Plumbing provides 24/7 emergency plumbing services throughout Dallas, Plano, and Frisco. Our technicians typically arrive within 60 minutes."
    }
  }]
}

Schema implementation tips:
- Use JSON-LD format — Google's preferred method.
- Include @id references to connect entities across your site.
- Match schema data exactly to visible page content.
- Validate with Google's Rich Results Test tool.
- Update schema whenever business information changes.

Content Strategy for Local Keywords

Your content strategy should target the full spectrum of local search queries.

Keyword categories for contractors:

Category Example Keywords Content Type
Service + city "plumber Dallas," "HVAC repair Plano" Location pages, service pages

Internal Linking for Local SEO

Internal linking helps Google discover your pages, distributes authority across your site, and keeps visitors engaged longer.

Internal linking structure for contractors:

Homepage

  │     ├── Plumbing Services

Internal linking rules:
- Link from your homepage to every major service and location page.
- Link from service pages to related location pages ("We also provide drain cleaning in Plano").
- Link from location pages to specific services offered in that city.
- Use descriptive anchor text ("emergency plumbing in Dallas" instead of "click here").
- Add a "Related Services" or "Areas We Serve" section to every page with 3-5 internal links.

Chapter 5: Local Link Building

Links from other websites to yours remain a powerful ranking signal. For local SEO, the quality and local relevance of links matter more than sheer quantity. A single link from your local Chamber of Commerce can be worth more than 50 links from random directories.

This chapter covers the link building strategies that work specifically for contractors and home service businesses.

Citation Building

Citations are mentions of your business name, address, and phone number on other websites. They do not always include a link, but they still signal credibility to Google.

Geo-specific directories Chamber of Commerce, city business directories, local blogs Highest local relevance signal

Chapter 6: Multi-Location Local SEO

If you operate multiple offices or serve multiple major markets, your local SEO strategy scales in complexity. One website with dedicated location pages outperforms separate websites for each location. This chapter covers how to manage local SEO across multiple service areas without diluting your authority.

Location Page Strategy

Each physical location needs its own dedicated landing page. These pages should not be copies of each other with swapped city names.

Multi-location page structure:

Homepage
  └── Locations
        ├── Dallas Office
        │     ├── Services in Dallas
        │     ├── Projects in Dallas
        │     └── Dallas Team
        ├── Plano Office
        │     ├── Services in Plano
        │     ├── Projects in Plano
        │     └── Plano Team
        └── Frisco Office
              ├── Services in Frisco
              ├── Projects in Frisco
              └── Frisco Team

URL structure best practices:

Approach Example Best For
Subdirectory /locations/dallas/ Most businesses — consolidates authority
Subdomain dallas.yoursite.com Very large franchises — technical complexity
Separate domains dallasplumbing.com Not recommended — splits authority

The subdirectory approach (/locations/city/) is best for 99% of multi-location home service businesses. It keeps all authority on one domain while allowing Google to understand your geographic coverage.

Unique content requirements per location page:
- Different team member photos and bios.
- Different customer testimonials.
- Different project photos from that city.
- Different local landmarks or neighborhood mentions.
- Different service area maps.
- Unique phone number (if available) or click-to-call tracking number.

GBP Management for Multiple Locations

Each physical location needs its own verified Google Business Profile. Never try to manage multiple addresses from one profile.

Multi-location GBP setup:

  1. Create separate profiles for each location with unique addresses.
  2. Use unique phone numbers if possible (local numbers outperform toll-free).
  3. Link each profile to its location page (/locations/dallas/), not your homepage.
  4. Use Google Business Profile Manager for bulk management if you have 10+ locations.

GBP Manager benefits:
- Manage all locations from one dashboard.
- Bulk upload photos, posts, and updates.
- Compare performance across locations.
- Delegate management to location managers.

Review management at scale:
- Assign a local manager or technician to respond to reviews for their location.
- Use a reputation management tool to monitor all locations centrally.
- Set response time goals (within 48 hours for all reviews).

Citation Management at Scale

Managing citations for 5, 10, or 50 locations requires systems and tools.

Citation management tools for multi-location businesses:

Tool Best For Price Range

BrightLocal Small to mid-size $100-300/month

The citation management process:
1. Create a master spreadsheet with NAP for every location.
2. Audit existing citations for accuracy using a tool.

4. Submit each location to major directories.

Local Content Scaling

Creating unique content for every location is the biggest challenge in multi-location SEO. Here is how to scale without sacrificing quality.

Content scaling strategies:

  1. Template with unique modules — Create a page template with sections that are standardized (service descriptions, process) and sections that are unique (local projects, team photos, neighborhood mentions).

  2. Local project showcases — Every completed project becomes content. Take photos, write 200 words about the job, and publish it on the relevant location page.

  3. City-specific FAQs — Each city has unique building codes, climate challenges, and regulations. Create FAQ sections that address city-specific concerns.

  4. Local partnership content — Feature local suppliers, community partners, or charities you support in each market.

  5. Customer stories by city — Interview satisfied customers in each market and publish their stories.

16-50 locations 1 per location + service area pages 8-15 pieces
50+ locations 1 per location + regional hubs 15-30 pieces

Chapter 7: Tracking and Measuring Local SEO

You cannot improve what you do not measure. Local SEO tracking goes far beyond "where do I rank?" This chapter covers the metrics, tools, and frameworks for measuring real business impact.

Rank Tracking Tools

Rank tracking tells you where your business appears in search results for target keywords.

What to track:

Metric Tool Why It Matters
Local Pack position BrightLocal, Local Falcon Direct visibility in the map results
Organic position Semrush, Ahrefs Website visibility below the map
Keyword rankings by city BrightLocal, Whitespark Performance across service areas
Grid ranking maps Local Falcon Visual map of rankings across a service area
Competitor rankings Semrush, Ahrefs Know who you are competing against

The grid ranking map: Local Falcon and similar tools show your ranking position across a grid of points in your service area. This reveals ranking "dead zones" where you are invisible and "hot zones" where you dominate.

[VISUAL: Grid ranking map showing color-coded positions across a city map]

GBP Insights Analysis

Google Business Profile Insights provides free data on how customers interact with your profile.

Key GBP metrics to monitor weekly:

Metric What It Measures Good Benchmark
Views How many times your profile appeared 2,000-5,000/month for active profiles
Discovery searches Views from non-branded queries 70%+ of total views
Direct searches Views from branded queries 30% or less (shows new customer acquisition)
Calls Phone calls from your profile 50-200/month depending on market
Direction requests Map direction clicks 20-100/month
Website clicks Clicks to your website 100-500/month
Photo views Engagement with your photos Track month-over-month growth

GBP Insights action framework:

  1. If discovery searches are low: Your profile is not matching enough search queries. Add more services, optimize categories, and improve your business description.
  2. If calls are low but views are high: Your profile is not compelling enough to generate action. Improve photos, add more reviews, and strengthen your CTA.
  3. If direction requests are high but calls are low: You might be attracting out-of-service-area traffic. Refine your service areas.
  4. If photo views are low: Upload more high-quality, geo-tagged photos.

Call Tracking

Call tracking lets you attribute phone calls to specific marketing channels. Without it, you are guessing which SEO efforts are working.

Call tracking for local SEO:

  2. GBP tracking number — Use a call tracking number on your Google Business Profile to measure calls specifically from local search.
  3. Location-specific numbers — Assign unique tracking numbers to each location page.

Chapter 8: Common Local SEO Mistakes

After auditing hundreds of contractor websites and Google Business Profiles, we see the same mistakes repeatedly. This chapter covers the 15 most common local SEO errors and exactly how to fix them.

15 Mistakes with Solutions

Mistake 1: Wrong primary GBP category

Problem Impact Fix
Choosing "Contractor" instead of "Plumber" or "HVAC contractor" Your profile never matches specific service searches Research top competitors' categories and select the most specific option

Mistake 2: Inconsistent NAP across the web

Problem Impact Fix
"St." vs. "Street," different phone formats, name variations Google cannot confirm your business identity Create a Single Source of Truth document and audit all listings

Mistake 3: No review generation system

Problem Impact Fix
Relying on customers to leave reviews voluntarily 5-10 reviews while competitors have 200+ Implement a post-service text message system with a direct review link

Mistake 4: Duplicate or unclaimed GBP listings

Problem Impact Fix
Multiple profiles for the same business split reviews and authority Confused customers, diluted rankings Claim all listings, merge duplicates through Google support

Mistake 5: Keyword-stuffed business name

Problem Impact Fix
"Johnson Plumbing — Best Plumber — Emergency Service — Drain Cleaning" GBP suspension risk, looks spammy Use your legal business name only; add keywords to description

Mistake 6: Thin or duplicate location pages

Problem Impact Fix
Swapping city names on a template with no unique content Google penalty, zero rankings Write unique content for each city with local proof

Mistake 7: Missing or incorrect schema markup

Problem Impact Fix
No LocalBusiness schema, or schema with wrong information Google cannot understand your business Implement JSON-LD schema and validate with Rich Results Test

Mistake 8: Ignoring GBP posts and Q&A

Problem Impact Fix
Inactive profile signals a dormant business Lower rankings, fewer engagement signals Post weekly updates; seed 10 Q&A items

Mistake 9: Using a personal address publicly

Problem Impact Fix
Residential address visible on GBP for a service-area business Competitor reports, policy violation Hide your address and define service areas by city/ZIP

Mistake 10: No dedicated service pages

Problem Impact Fix
One generic "Services" page with a bullet list Misses "service + city" search opportunities Create individual pages for each service

Mistake 11: Poor photo quality or quantity

Problem Impact Fix
Stock photos or no photos on GBP 42% fewer direction requests, lower engagement Upload 20+ real project photos with geo-tags

Mistake 12: Not responding to reviews

Problem Impact Fix
Unanswered reviews signal poor customer service 97% of consumers read responses; unanswered negatives hurt trust Respond to every review within 48 hours

Mistake 13: Unrealistic service areas

Problem Impact Fix
Claiming to serve an entire state from one location Spam flag, profile suspension Limit service areas to a realistic 1-2 hour radius

Mistake 14: No call tracking or conversion measurement

Problem Impact Fix
Cannot prove SEO is working Budget cuts, missed optimization opportunities Implement call tracking and lead attribution

Mistake 15: Copying brick-and-mortar SEO tactics

Problem Impact Fix
Optimizing for foot traffic, public address, storefront amenities Wasted effort on irrelevant signals Focus on prominence, reviews, and service-area relevance

Service-Area Specific Errors

Service-area businesses face unique pitfalls that storefront businesses do not.

Error: Listing as a storefront when you are a service-area business
If customers cannot visit your office, you must hide your address. A visible address on a service-area business is a policy violation that competitors can report.

Error: Using a virtual office or P.O. Box
Google requires a legitimate physical location where you conduct business. Virtual offices and P.O. Boxes will get your profile suspended.

Error: Rapid profile changes
Updating your name, address, phone, and category within a short timeframe triggers Google's spam detection. Make changes gradually and document why each change is necessary.

Multi-Location Pitfalls

Error: One GBP for multiple locations
Each physical address needs its own profile. Using one profile for multiple offices violates Google's guidelines.

Error: Duplicate content across location pages
Google penalizes pages with substantially similar content. Every location page needs unique photos, testimonials, and local references.

Error: Linking all GBPs to the homepage
Each location's GBP should link to its dedicated location page, not your homepage. This strengthens the connection between the profile and the relevant geographic content.

GBP Suspension Risks

Google suspends Business Profiles for policy violations. A suspended profile disappears from search entirely.

Common suspension triggers:
- Fake or virtual office address
- Keyword-stuffed business name
- Multiple profiles for the same business
- Business type mismatch (e.g., claiming a residential home as a storefront)
- Rapid, suspicious profile changes
- Fake reviews or review manipulation
- Business does not exist at the listed address

If your profile is suspended:
1. Do not create a new profile.
2. Review Google's Business Profile guidelines.
3. Fix the violation.
4. Submit a reinstatement request through Google Business Profile Help.
5. Provide documentation (business license, utility bill, lease agreement).
6. Wait 1-3 weeks for a response.

Schema Markup Advanced

Beyond basic LocalBusiness schema, advanced markup types can unlock rich results and AI citations.

Advanced schema types for contractors:

Schema Type Where to Use Benefit
FAQPage Service pages, location pages Rich results, AI Overview eligibility
HowTo DIY guides, maintenance checklists Step-by-step rich results

Schema stacking example:

On a service page, combine Service + LocalBusiness + FAQPage + Review schema for maximum visibility:

{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@graph": [
    { "@type": "Service", ... },
    { "@type": "Plumber", ... },
    { "@type": "FAQPage", ... },
    { "@type": "AggregateRating", ... }
  ]
}

Local Content Clusters

Content clusters build topical authority by creating a network of related content around a central topic.

Example cluster for an HVAC company:

Pillar page: "Complete HVAC Services in Dallas"
  ├── "AC Repair in Dallas: What Homeowners Need to Know"
  ├── "Furnace Installation Costs in Dallas (2026)"
  ├── "Dallas HVAC Maintenance Plans: Are They Worth It?"
  ├── "Why Is My AC Blowing Hot Air? [Dallas Homeowner's Guide]"

Cluster benefits:

- Provides AI systems with comprehensive topic coverage.

Video SEO for Local

Video content is underutilized by contractors and represents a massive opportunity.

Video types that rank:

Video Type Platform Optimization
Project walkthroughs YouTube Title: "[Service] in [City] — [Project Type]"
Customer testimonials YouTube, GBP Geo-tagged, location in title
How-to guides YouTube Target "how to [task] in [city]"
Before/after reveals YouTube, Instagram Location hashtags, local keywords
Team introductions YouTube, website Humanize your brand

YouTube optimization for local SEO:
1. Include your city in the video title.
2. Write a 200+ word description with local keyw

ords.
3. Add location tags and relevant hashtags.
4. Embed videos on relevant service and location pages.
5. Create a YouTube channel trailer optimized for your primary service area.

Pro tip: Google often surfaces YouTube videos in the Local Pack and organic results for "how to" queries. A video titled "How to Unclog a Drain in Dallas" can rank for both local and informational searches.

Voice Search Optimization

Voice search accounts for 20%+ of mobile searches and is growing rapidly. Voice queries are conversational and question-based.

Voice search optimization tactics:

  1. Target question keywords: "Who is the best plumber in Dallas?" instead of "best plumber Dallas."
  2. Write conversational content: Use natural language that matches how people speak.
  3. Create FAQ sections: Voice assistants pull answers from FAQ schema.
  4. Optimize for "near me": Include "near me" variations naturally in content.
  5. Focus on featured snippets: Voice assistants often read featured snippet content aloud.

Voice search content framework:

Question: [Exact voice query]
Direct answer: [40-60 word concise answer]
Expanded explanation: [2-3 paragraphs of detail]
Related questions: [3-5 follow-up questions with answers]

AI Overview Optimization

AI Overviews now appear in 40.16% of local queries, according to 2025 data. When an AI Overview appears, it can reduce organic click-through rates by 47-61%. But it also creates an opportunity: if your content is cited in the AI Overview, you get visibility even if the user never clicks.

GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) for contractors:

Tactic Implementation
Clear definitions Start every major section with "[Topic] is..."
Structured answers Use lists, tables, and step-by-step formats
Entity optimization Clearly define your business entity with schema
Citation-ready content Include statistics, expert quotes, and specific data
FAQ schema Mark up all common questions
Conversational tone Write how people ask questions to AI

The AI citation formula:

Google's AI compiles answers from sources that are clear, authoritative, and directly relevant. To earn AI citations:

  1. Answer questions directly in the first 1-2 sentences of every section.
  2. Use specific data — "46% of Google searches have local intent" is more citable than "many searches are local."
  3. Build topical authority — Cover every subtopic related to your services.
  4. Earn brand mentions — AI systems reference businesses that are widely mentioned as experts.
  5. Maintain consistent NAP — AI systems cross-reference multiple sources to verify business information.

  3. Week 3: Implement a review generation system.
  4. Week 4: Create dedicated service pages on your website.
  5. Week 5: Build top 20 citations.
  6. Week 6: Add LocalBusiness schema markup.
  7. Week 7: Create location pages for your top 3 cities.
  8. Week 8: Start weekly GBP posts.
  9. Week 9: Join your local Chamber of Commerce.
  10. Week 10: Seed your GBP Q&A section.
  11. Week 11: Launch a local sponsorship.
  12. Week 12: Set up call tracking and measure ROI.

When to Hire an Agency

DIY local SEO works if you have 5-10 hours per week and are willing to learn. But there are signs it is time to hire help:

Sign What It Means
You have 5+ locations Complexity exceeds DIY capacity
You are too busy to post weekly Consistency matters more than perfection
Your rankings have stalled for 6+ months You need fresh strategy and advanced tactics
You are losing to competitors with worse reviews They have better technical SEO or more citations
You want to scale aggressively An agency brings systems and experience
You do not understand schema, tracking, or analytics Technical gaps limit your potential

What to look for in a local SEO agency:
- Home service industry experience
- Case studies with measurable results
- Transparent reporting on rankings, traffic, and leads
- No long-term contracts (month-to-month is standard)
- Clear pricing and scope of work
- References from other contractors

Red flags:
- Guarantees of #1 rankings (impossible to guarantee)
- Packages under $500/month (not enough time for real work)
- No reporting or vague metrics
- Black hat tactics (fake reviews, keyword stuffing, link schemes)
- No understanding of service-area business differences

FAQ Section

What is local SEO for contractors?

Local SEO for contractors is the practice of optimizing your online presence to appear in local search results when homeowners search for services you provide. It includes optimizing your Google Business Profile, building local citations, generating reviews, creating location-specific website content, and earning local backlinks. For service-area businesses like contractors, local SEO focuses on prominence and relevance rather than just proximity to the searcher.

How long does local SEO take to work for a home service business?

You can see initial improvements in 30-60 days by completing your Google Business Profile and fixing basic issues. Meaningful ranking improvements typically take 3-6 months of consistent effort. Full competitive dominance in your market usually requires 6-12 months. The timeline depends on your market's competition, your starting point, and how aggressively you implement the strategies in this guide. Emergency and high-intent keywords often improve faster than broad informational terms.

How do I rank higher on Google Maps as a contractor?

To rank higher on Google Maps, focus on the top three ranking factors: (1) Choose the most specific primary business category for your trade, (2) Generate 10+ new Google reviews per month with text content, and (3) Complete every field in your Google Business Profile including services, photos, posts, and Q&A. Additionally, ensure your website has dedicated service pages optimized for your primary city, implement LocalBusiness schema markup, and build consistent citations across major directories.

Do I need a physical office to rank in local search?

No. Service-area businesses can rank effectively without a public storefront. You need a legitimate physical address for GBP verification, but you can hide it from public view and define your service areas by city or ZIP code. Google understands that plumbers, HVAC technicians, and roofers travel to customers' homes. Your ranking depends more on prominence (reviews, citations, links) and relevance (categories, services, content) than on having a visible office.

How many Google reviews do I need?

Aim for a minimum of 50 Google reviews to establish credibility and improve Local Pack visibility. The top-ranking businesses in most markets have 200+ reviews. Quality matters as much as quantity — reviews with detailed text, recent dates, and mentions of specific services carry more weight than one-word reviews. A steady velocity of 10-20 new reviews per month signals an active, trusted business to Google's algorithm.

What is the best primary category for my Google Business Profile?

Choose the most specific category that matches your core service. If you are a plumber, use "Plumber" not "Contractor." If you are an HVAC company, use "HVAC contractor" not "Home services." Search your target keywords and look at what categories the top three Local Pack results use. Your primary category is the single most important ranking factor, so research this carefully before committing.

Should I create separate location pages for every city I serve?

Create dedicated location pages for your top 5-10 cities where you actively work. For smaller surrounding towns, group 2-3 nearby communities on a single service area page. Each location page needs genuinely unique content — not just a swapped city name. Include local project photos, testimonials from that city, neighborhood mentions, and city-specific service details. Thin or duplicate location pages will hurt your rankings.

How do I get more local backlinks?

The most effective local link building strategies for contractors are: (1) Join your local Chamber of Commerce for a directory backlink, (2) Get listed on manufacturer "Find a Pro" pages if you are a certified dealer, (3) Sponsor local youth sports teams or charity events, (4) Pitch stories to local media about home maintenance topics, and (5) Create linkable assets like cost calculators or neighborhood home value reports. Focus on relevance over raw authority.

What is NAP consistency and why does it matter?

NAP stands for Name, Address, Phone number. NAP consistency means your business information matches character-for-character across your website, Google Business Profile, and every directory listing. Even minor variations like "St." versus "Street" can confuse search engines and dilute your authority. Inconsistent NAP is one of the most common reasons contractors struggle to rank. Create a Single Source of Truth document and copy from it for every new listing.

How do I respond to negative reviews?

Respond to negative reviews within 24-48 hours using this formula: (1) Acknowledge the customer's experience and apologize, (2) Briefly explain without being defensive, (3) Take the conversation offline by providing a direct contact, and (4) Offer to make it right. Never argue publicly, blame the customer, or discuss specific contract details. A professional response to a negative review can actually increase trust with future customers — 97% of consumers read business responses.

What schema markup should contractors use?

Every contractor should implement at least three schema types: (1) LocalBusiness schema (or a specific subtype like Plumber or HVACBusiness) on your homepage and location pages, (2) Service schema on every service page, and (3) FAQPage schema on pages with frequently asked questions. Advanced options include Review/AggregateRating schema for star ratings in search results, HowTo schema for maintenance guides, and BreadcrumbList schema for navigation.

How do I track local SEO ROI?

Track these metrics monthly: (1) Google Business Profile Insights (views, calls, direction requests), (2) keyword rankings for target terms in each city, (3) organic traffic from local search queries, (4) phone calls from local search using call tracking, (5) form submissions attributed to organic/local search, and (6) total revenue from local SEO leads. Calculate cost per lead and compare to other marketing channels. Local SEO typically delivers 500%+ ROI for home service businesses.

Can I do local SEO myself or should I hire an agency?

You can absolutely do local SEO yourself if you have 5-10 hours per week and are willing to learn. The fundamentals — GBP optimization, review generation, citation building, and basic on-page SEO — are learnable for any business owner. Hire an agency when you have 5+ locations, your rankings have stalled despite DIY efforts, you are too busy to maintain consistency, or you need advanced tactics like schema implementation and link building at scale.

What are the biggest local SEO mistakes contractors make?

The top five mistakes are: (1) Choosing the wrong primary GBP category, (2) Having inconsistent NAP information across the web, (3) Not actively generating reviews, (4) Creating thin or duplicate location pages, and (5) Ignoring Google Business Profile posts and Q&A. These mistakes are easy to fix but cost contractors thousands in lost leads every month they go unaddressed.

How does AI Overview affect local SEO for contractors?

AI Overviews now appear in over 40% of local queries and can reduce organic click-through rates. However, they also create opportunities. To optimize for AI Overviews, structure your content with clear definitions, direct answers, FAQ schema, and structured data. Google's AI prioritizes businesses with complete GBP profiles, consistent citations, recent reviews, and authoritative website content. Contractors who optimize for AI visibility now will have a significant advantage as AI search grows.

What is the difference between service-area and brick-and-mortar SEO?

Service-area businesses (contractors, HVAC, plumbing) optimize for prominence and relevance because they travel to customers. Brick-and-mortar businesses (retail, restaurants) optimize heavily for proximity because customers visit their location. Service-area businesses hide their address on GBP, define service areas by city/ZIP, and focus on reviews and citations. Brick-and-mortar businesses display their address publicly, optimize for foot traffic, and focus on local amenities and hours.

How often should I post on my Google Business Profile?

Post at least once per week. Businesses that post weekly see 70% more engagement than those posting monthly or less. Each post expires after seven days, so consistency is key. Share project updates, seasonal offers, maintenance tips, and community involvement. Include a photo with every post and use the appropriate call-to-action button.

Do Yelp and other review platforms matter?

Google reviews are the most important by far, but a diverse review profile builds trust. Yelp carries high domain authority and is trusted by consumers researching service businesses. The Better Business Bureau adds credibility, especially for older demographics. Facebook reviews are easy to generate and visible to social media users. Industry-specific platforms like Angi and Thumbtack matter for trade-specific credibility. Focus 80% of your effort on Google, then diversify.

What is the best way to get reviews from customers?

The most effective method is asking in person immediately after completing a satisfying job, followed by a text message with a direct review link within 2-4 hours. Train every technician to ask every satisfied customer. Use simple scripts like: "If you were happy with our work today, would you mind leaving us a quick Google review? It really helps other homeowners find us." Make the process frictionless with a short, direct link.

How do I optimize for "near me" searches?

To optimize for "near me" searches: (1) Ensure your Google Business Profile is fully optimized with accurate service areas, (2) Include "near me" variations naturally in your website content, (3) Add location-specific schema markup, (4) Build local citations that confirm your geographic relevance, (5) Generate reviews that mention neighborhoods and cities, and (6) Create location pages for each major service area. Google uses proximity, relevance, and prominence to determine "near me" results.

Conclusion: Your Path to Local Search Domination

Local SEO is not a one-time project. It is a system that compounds over time. The contractors who dominate local search are not necessarily the ones with the biggest budgets. They are the ones who show up consistently — posting weekly, generating reviews monthly, building citations quarterly, and creating content that answers real homeowner questions.

Key Takeaways

  • Your Google Business Profile is your most important asset. A complete profile gets 7 times more clicks than an incomplete one.
  • Reviews are both a ranking factor and a conversion tool. Aim for 50+ reviews with a 4.2-4.5 star rating to build trust and visibility.
  • NAP consistency across every online mention of your business is non-negotiable. Create a Single Source of Truth and audit quarterly.
  • Dedicated service pages and location pages are the foundation of on-page local SEO. Never rely on a single "Services" page.
  • Local link building is about relationships, not shortcuts. Join your Chamber, sponsor a team, and get listed by your manufacturers.
  • Track leads and revenue, not just rankings. Local SEO typically delivers 500%+ ROI when measured properly.
  • AI search is changing the game. Optimize for AI Overviews with clear definitions, structured answers, and comprehensive topic coverage.

Your Next Steps

In the next 24 hours, claim and verify your Google Business Profile if you have not already. In the next week, complete every field in your profile and fix any NAP inconsistencies. In the next month, implement a review generation system and create your first dedicated service page. In the next 90 days, follow the action plan in Chapter 10 and measure your results.

The market share is sitting unclaimed. Most of your competitors have incomplete profiles, inconsistent citations, and no review system. The bar is lower than you think. Execute consistently for 90 days, and you will outrank businesses that have been coasting for years.

The homeowners in your service area are searching right now. Will they find you?
